transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The midterm elections are about two weeks away.
These are the most expensive ever.
NPR Stephen Fowler tells us more than $15 billion have been raised
to try to influence voters to choose candidates.
>> There's a ton of Democratic nominees in House and Senate races
that are receiving just gobsmacking amounts
of donations, but the Democratic Party, capital D,
capital P, is unpopular.
You know who else is unpopular?
Republicans right now.
Thanks to the war in Iran and rising gas prices,
uncertainty about the economy.
So you've got a few mega donors giving a few super PACs a lot
of money to try and convince voters to elect Republicans anyway.
>> NPR Stephen Fowler reporting.
President Trump will travel to Wichita, Kansas today.
He'll campaign for Republican U.S. Senator Roger Marshall.
The incumbent Marshall is in a close race
against Democrat Adam Hamilton for the seat.
President Trump says Israel's embattled Prime Minister has his
complete and total endorsement in upcoming Israeli elections.
The endorsement is a boost for Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu.
NPR's Emily Fang reports Netanyahu is facing serious
questions about his handling of several wars.
>> Citing Israel's support for the ongoing war in Iran,
Trump wrote that without Netanyahu,
America would, quote, "have to do this work ourselves."
Netanyahu responded by video that he was honored and humbled.
And he needs all the political help he can get
as Israel prepares to vote at the end of the month.
The latest polls show Netanyahu trailing behind opposition
candidate Gaddy Eisenkot.
Recent reporting also alleges Netanyahu ignored repeated
warnings from various Arab intelligence officials
before Hamas attacked Israel on October 7th, 2023.
Netanyahu's managed to survive criticism of that
security failure.
But that and the fallout from Israel's war in Gaza has turned
this election into one of the most consequential
in Israel's history.
Emily Fang in Pure News, Washington.
>> Russia's foreign minister met his Saudi Arabian counterpart
today ahead of a visit to Iran.
This comes as Iran backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia
trade attacks, and PR's Ayyab Batrawi reports.
>> Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and Saudi Foreign
Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan met Sunday in neighboring
Bahrain, where they discussed the war in Yemen,
according to official statements by both sides.
Russia's TASS news agency reports that Lavrov said
during the meeting that Houthi attacks on civilian
infrastructure in Saudi Arabia are unacceptable.
Lavrov also met with foreign ministers from Gulf Arab states
while in Bahrain to discuss the situation in the Strait of
Hormuz and the Red Sea's Babin Mende.
Lavrov is meeting Iran's president and foreign minister
next into Tehran Monday.
Lavrov told Iran state broadcaster ahead of the visit
that Russia is prepared to help Iran restart nuclear
talks with the U.S.
Ayyab Batrawi and Pure News, Dubai.
>> You're listening to NPR.
President Trump says his plan renovations to a Washington,
D.C. golf course will begin immediately.
Writing online last hour, Trump dismissed opponents who
filed suit to stop him.
A federal judge has ordered a halt to any renovation work
while the suit is heard.
Trump called the judge, quote, "a crazed lunatic."
Trump says the Interior Department is going ahead
with the work because they don't need an approval.
It is not clear that is true.
The A.I. Company anthropic says it is setting up a public
benefit fund for charitable donations.
The company is committing 5% of its shares to the fund.
NPR's John Rooich reports this comes as anthropic prepares
for an initial public offering.
>> After raising money in May, anthropic said it was valued
at close to a trillion dollars.
And some analysts say the IPO could double that.
So the new anthropic public benefit fund will be
substantial, and the company says more shares will go
into the fund as anthropic's valuation grows.
As for the kind of donations that the fund could make,
anthropic says an example could be in the labor market,
which many experts expect A.I. to disrupt.
Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying
and addressing the challenge.
The new fund, it says, could enable the company
to take bolder action.
John Rooich, NPR News.
>> What's known as the leap second is now canceled.
The international authority responsible
for timekeeping adds a leap second from time to time,
just like a leap year every four years.
Instead, they will wait for the right time to add a leap hour.
But that might not happen for centuries.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Midterm election campaign spending exceeds $15 billion as Republicans face unpopularity amid Iran war
President Trump to campaign in Wichita, Kansas for Republican Senator Roger Marshall
Trump endorses Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israeli elections as Netanyahu trails opponent Gaddy Eisenkot
Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov meets Saudi counterpart in Bahrain over Yemen war and Houthi attacks
Trump says Washington, D.C. golf course renovations will begin despite federal judge's halt order
Anthropic creates public benefit fund pledging 5% of shares for charitable donations ahead of IPO
International timekeeping authority cancels leap second, opting instead for a future leap hour
